$comment: GROUND-TRUTH TEMPLATE for the $5 screen, NOT ground truth. Shape: tools/fixtures/golden-tt-7679960172495785246.json and the tools/pack-eval/score.ts Fixture type, extended with the source-claim contract from PROMPTS-AND-CONTRACTS.md (prescribed vs demonstrated, provenance said/seen/written). Everything filled in here came from text this repo actually fetched — the platform caption and, where the platform publishes one, the free ASR WebVTT. NOBODY HAS WATCHED THIS VIDEO. No frame was extracted, no AI call was made, nothing was saved in the app. Every TODO_REVIEW is a decision for the human reviewer, and a visible count is never one of the things text alone can decide.
$visual: score.ts reads this: 'unavailable' means nobody looked and the card must carry no visual claim (score.ts:459-470). A carousel has no video, so the video path is unavailable even though slides exist.

source_claims.$note: An ascending ladder applied to every movement each round. It is ONE session-scoped scheme, not five separate rep claims per exercise, and the trailing ellipsis means it continues past 20 — record that the top of the range is open, not 20.

$source_claims: reader-v2 claim shape: field, value, scope, source_kind, quote. A claim here is the CREATOR'S instruction, never an observation and never a recommendation.

reviewer_checklist: Watch the whole video once before writing anything down.
Enumerate occurrences in chronological order, including repeats and both sides; repeats are separate occurrences even when the name matches.
For every occurrence set demonstrated.count to a number ONLY if continuous evidence shows every counted cycle. Otherwise leave 'unknown'.
Write acceptable_canonical_ids before you see any model output.
Record t0/t1 as the boundary you would accept plus uncertainty_s, not a point you had to guess.
Mark any claim you cannot resolve from the source as unresolvable rather than choosing the likely answer.
The rep count CHANGES every round. Record the per-round dose per occurrence, and make sure the ladder is not flattened to a single number.
Caption is Spanish-adjacent CrossFit shorthand. Keep the quote in the source language; translate only the label.
(100/70) must end up as a load, in kg, with two scopes — not as reps and not as a percentage.
